pointers.sentence: The nonce is how a page names the inline elements it means: the policy lists it as `'nonce-…'`, and the browser runs an inline script or style only if its `"nonce"` attribute matches (`docs/ref/csp.txt`).
Django had no content security policy before 6.0, which brought the middleware, the two settings, the `csp` context processor and the decorators (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
`{% csp_nonce_attr %}` and the nonce on the elements of Django's own templates came in 6.1 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

`SECURE_CSP` and `SECURE_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` are each a dictionary from a directive (`"script-src"`) to the sources it allows, and each defaults to an empty dictionary, which adds no header (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

A value that is neither `None` nor a dictionary is refused by `"security.E026"`, with or without `--deploy` ([The security checks](checks.md)) (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_csp_settings`).
And `CSP.NONCE`, `"<CSP_NONCE_SENTINEL>"`, is Django's own: a placeholder that stands in a directive's list for the nonce until the header is written (`django/utils/csp.py:CSP`).

`build_policy` turns one dictionary and a nonce into the text of one header: each directive followed by its sources, the directives in the dictionary's order joined with `"; "` (`django/utils/csp.py:build_policy`).

`LazyNonce` is a `SimpleLazyObject` around `generate_nonce`, which returns `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`, sixteen random bytes as 22 characters of URL-safe base64 (`django/utils/csp.py:generate_nonce`).
`LazyNonce.__bool__` answers instead whether the value has been made, and makes nothing (`django/utils/csp.py:LazyNonce`).

The `csp` context processor adds `"csp_nonce"` to the context, the request's nonce or `None` (`django/template/context_processors.py:csp`) ([The context: `Context`, `RequestContext` and context processors](../templates/context.md)).

`{% csp_nonce_attr %}` writes `nonce="…"` from it, or nothing; given a form's `Media`, the stylesheets and scripts the form requires, it writes their elements, the nonce, when there is one, on all but those given as ready HTML (`django/utils/csp.py:nonce_attr`) ([The built-in tags](../templates/tags.md), [Form assets: `Media`](../forms/media.md)).
Django's own templates carry the tag on their `<script>`, `<style>` and `<link>` elements, all but the debug pages (`django/contrib/admin/templates/`, `django/views/templates/csrf_403.html`).
Django's own templates carry the tag on their `<script>`, `<style>` and `<link>` elements, all but the debug pages (`django/contrib/admin/templates/`, `django/views/templates/csrf_403.html`).

The built-in CSRF failure page, which `csrf_failure` renders with an `Engine` of its own, is given the nonce by the view itself ([The CSRF check: `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`](csrf-check.md)) (`django/views/csrf.py:csrf_failure`).

Without the processor a template's context holds the nonce only where other code puts it, and unless other code reads it the header names none; `"security.W027"` warns of that only where no template engine lists it ([The security checks](checks.md)) (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_csp_nonce_context_processor`).

`ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_request` puts a new `LazyNonce` on the request as `"_csp_nonce"`, which costs nothing while no value is drawn (`django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_request`).
`get_nonce` reads it back, or gives `None` for a request the middleware has not seen (`django/middleware/csp.py:get_nonce`).
Otherwise the header is `build_policy` of the policy and the request's nonce, the same nonce for both headers (`django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_response`).

A policy that is not a dictionary is refused with `TypeError` when the decorator is made, before there is a view to wrap (`django/views/decorators/csp.py:_make_csp_decorator`) ([View decorators](../views/decorators.md)).

An empty dictionary, then, takes the setting's place like any other policy, and so exempts a view from that decorator's header (`django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_response`).

Django's debug pages, whose styles are written into them, carry both decorators with `{}` ([The debug pages and `ExceptionReporter`](../views/debug.md)) (`django/views/debug.py:technical_500_response`, `django/views/debug.py:technical_404_response`, `django/views/debug.py:default_urlconf`).

A view that raises, `Http404` say, is answered by the handler's exception handling, with a response that carries no mark of the view's: with `settings.DEBUG` off, a view under `csp_override({})` that raises `Http404` is answered with a 404 under the site's policy (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
